headline: Apple is profitable again
text: At the Macworld show on 6 January Apple announced that it expects a profit of more than 45 million dollars on sales of about 1.575 billion for the quarter to December, its first good news in years. Jobs has cut the product line, ended the licensing of the Mac to clone makers and opened an online store.
source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320193/0000320193-98-000001.txt (Apple 8-K with press release of 6 January 1998, read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Apple_Inc. (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The iMac G3, introduced in August 1998

headline: Amazon buys bookstores in Britain and Germany, splits its shares
text: On April 27 Amazon reported sales of $87.4 million for the first quarter, up 446% from a year earlier, and a net loss of $9.3 million. It has more than 2.26 million customer accounts. It announced a two-for-one share split and the purchase of online booksellers in the UK and Germany and of the Internet Movie Database.
imageCaption: An Amazon warehouse in Germany, seen from the air

headline: Vickers accepts BMW's bid for Rolls-Royce
text: Vickers has accepted BMW's offer for the British luxury car maker Rolls-Royce Motor Cars, which already uses BMW engines; the price is 340 million pounds. Pischetsrieder promised to invest 1 billion pounds, double the workforce and triple production. Volkswagen is preparing a higher offer.
source: BBC News, 'BMW pledges £1bn Rolls-Royce investment', 7 April 1998, http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/business/71404.stm (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolls-Royce_Motors (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: A Rolls-Royce Silver Seraph, the model Rolls-Royce launched in 1998

headline: Daimler-Benz and Chrysler agree to merge
text: On 7 May Daimler-Benz and the American car maker Chrysler signed a contract to merge into DaimlerChrysler, a deal valued at about 38 billion dollars, the largest cross-border merger ever. Schrempp calls it a merger of equals. The new company will build Mercedes, Chrysler, Jeep and Dodge cars.
source: Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 1998 ('Merger: contract signed with Chrysler', 7 May 1998), https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/1998.xhtml?oid=4912914 (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercedes-Benz_Group (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: Jürgen Schrempp, chairman of Daimler-Benz, 1993

headline: Schweizerischer Bankverein leaves the market
text: Merged with Bankgesellschaft into UBS; holders received 1 1/13 UBS shares per Bankverein share. The shares are no longer traded.

headline: UBS is born
text: The merger of the Bankgesellschaft and the Bankverein took legal effect on 27-28 June. The new UBS has total assets of more than $590 billion, making it the second-largest bank in the world. Each Bankverein share becomes 1 1/13 UBS shares and each Bankgesellschaft bearer share five shares of the new bank.
source: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schweizerische_Bankgesellschaft (read 2026-10-03); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UBS (read 2026-10-03); share terms: data/src/universe.ts and data/manual/ubs.csv header (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: UBS at the Paradeplatz, Zurich

headline: Enron bids for Britain's Wessex Water
text: Enron is forming a global water company and has made an all-cash offer for Wessex Water, a British water utility, valued at about $2.9 billion. Enron believes water is the next utility market to be opened to competition.
imageCaption: Wessex Water's headquarters in Bath, England

headline: Russia defaults and the crisis goes global
text: On 17 August Russia devalued the rouble, defaulted on its domestic debt and stopped paying foreign creditors, a month after a $22.6 billion IMF and World Bank package. The Asian crisis and falling commodity prices had drained its reserves. Investors are fleeing risky markets everywhere.
imageCaption: Russian president Boris Yeltsin with IMF chief Michel Camdessus

headline: Yen at an eight-year low, Japan's banks under siege
text: The dollar reached 147 yen on 11 August, the yen's weakest in about eight years. Shares of the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan have fallen by more than 70% this summer as its bad loans came out; a planned rescue merger with Sumitomo Trust is faltering. Japan's economy is shrinking. In June the US Treasury and Federal Reserve sold $833 million for yen to slow its fall, with little lasting effect.
imageCaption: The Bank of Japan's head office, Tokyo

headline: UBS caught in the LTCM collapse
text: Long-Term Capital Management's equity fell from $2.3 billion to about $400 million in three weeks; on 23 September the New York Fed organised a $3.625 billion rescue by 14 banks, UBS among those putting in $300 million. UBS has its own large exposure through an option deal on LTCM shares struck in 1997. On 30 September UBS shares fell 14% in a day as investors lost confidence in the leadership; an internal investigation is due to report on Friday.
source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-Term_Capital_Management (read 2026-10-03); Neue Zürcher Zeitung, 1 October 1998, p. 35 ('Weitere Verluste der UBS-Valoren'), scan data/manual/scans/nzz/NZZ_1998-10-01.pdf (read 2026-10-03); https://www.encyclopedia.com/books/politics-and-business-magazines/ubs-ag (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The UBS trading building in Stamford, Connecticut

headline: eBay, the online auction site, goes public
text: eBay of San Jose sold 3.5 million shares on the Nasdaq at $18 each; on the first day they closed at about $53, valuing the company at nearly $1.9 billion. eBay runs a website where people auction goods to each other, from Beanie Babies to collectibles, and takes a fee on each sale. It had more than 1 million registered users at the end of August and, unlike most internet companies, it makes a profit.
imageCaption: Pierre Omidyar, eBay's founder

headline: Citicorp and Travelers become Citigroup
text: The merger of Citicorp, owner of Citibank, and Travelers Group, owner of the Travelers insurance business and the brokerage Salomon Smith Barney, was completed on 8 October, creating Citigroup, the world's largest financial services company. John Reed of Citicorp and Sanford Weill of Travelers run it together as co-chairmen and co-chief executives. Combining a bank with an insurer breaks the Depression-era Glass-Steagall rules; the Federal Reserve has granted a temporary waiver, and the company expects Congress to change the law. Salomon closed its bond arbitrage desk in July and was among the firms that put money into the rescue of the hedge fund Long-Term Capital Management in September.
imageCaption: Sandy Weill, head of Travelers and, with John Reed, of the merged Citigroup

headline: The yen leaps; Japan nationalises a failing bank
text: On 7 October the dollar fell from about 134 to 120 yen, the biggest daily move since the yen began to float in 1973, as hedge funds wound down bets financed with cheap yen. It fell to about 117 by the month's end. On 23 October the Diet nationalised the Long-Term Credit Bank under a new law that also offers public money to sound banks.
imageCaption: Head office of the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan, Tokyo

headline: A surprise Fed cut on 15 October and shares bounce 8 percent
text: Shares fell further in early October, then on 15 October the Federal Reserve cut its key rate again, to about 5 percent, without waiting for a meeting. The market rallied strongly after mid-October as fears of a financial breakdown eased. The S&P 500 rose 8% in October to 1,098.67.
imageCaption: Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan meets President Clinton and Vice President Gore in the Oval Office, 1993

headline: Nokia passes Motorola as the world's biggest phone maker
text: On 23 October Nokia reported third-quarter pre-tax profit up 85% and sales up 62%, far better than expected, and said it is now the world's largest maker of mobile phones, ahead of Motorola. Sales rose in the US, Europe and China.
imageCaption: The Nokia 5110, 1998

headline: DaimlerChrysler shares start trading
text: The merger was completed on 17 November and the new DaimlerChrysler share began trading in Frankfurt and New York. Daimler-Benz shareholders had approved the deal with 99.9% in September. Stock markets have recovered from the summer's Russian crisis.
source: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daimler-Benz (merger on 17 November 1998, read 2026-10-03); Mercedes-Benz Classic, Illustrated Chronicle 1998 (Extraordinary General Meeting, 17 September 1998), https://mercedes-benz-publicarchive.com/marsClassic/en/instance/ko/1998.xhtml?oid=4912914 (read 2026-10-03)
imageCaption: The Mercedes-Benz headquarters at the Untertürkheim plant, Stuttgart

headline: The Master Settlement: 206 billion dollars to the states
text: On 23 November the four largest US cigarette makers, Philip Morris, R.J. Reynolds, Brown & Williamson and Lorillard, signed the Master Settlement Agreement with 46 states and several territories. They will pay at least 206 billion dollars over the first 25 years and accept limits on marketing; in return the states drop their claims for smoking-related health costs.
imageCaption: State attorneys general who sued the tobacco industry ;;

headline: Siemens plans to spin off its chip business
text: On 4 November Siemens said it will spin off its semiconductor division and sell other units, as part of a plan to raise profits presented by chief executive von Pierer. The chip division lost 1.2 billion marks before tax in the year to September as chip prices collapsed; group sales rose 10% to 117.8 billion marks and Siemens takes a 4 billion mark restructuring charge.
imageCaption: Siemens' semiconductor business is based in the Munich suburb of Neubiberg; the campus shown was photographed in 2020

headline: theglobe.com rises 606% on its first day
text: theglobe.com, a website for online communities, went public on 13 November at 9 dollars a share; it touched 97 and closed at 63.50, a first-day gain of 606%. Internet shares are surging after the autumn's market scare: eBay more than doubled in November and Amazon rose about half. The Nasdaq, which first closed above 2,000 in July, rose 10% this month.

headline: Exxon and Mobil agree to merge
text: On 1 December Exxon agreed to buy Mobil in a share deal valued at about 76 to 79 billion dollars, the biggest US corporate combination ever: each Mobil share becomes 1.32015 Exxon shares, and Exxon's owners will hold about 70 percent. The deal reunites two pieces of Rockefeller's Standard Oil and needs regulators' approval. With crude below 11 dollars a barrel, the companies plan to cut 9,000 jobs and save 2.8 billion dollars a year. Lee Raymond will run the combined company.
imageCaption: The Exxon Mobil office tower in Houston, Texas

headline: Asia's crisis forces Boeing to cut production
text: On 1 December Boeing said it will cut production of the 747 from 3.5 to 2 planes a month in late 1999, and possibly to 1, and slow the 757, 767 and 777 too. 'The economic slowdown in Asia is driving air traffic down,' said Alan Mulally, head of commercial airplanes.
imageCaption: The Boeing 747 jumbo jet, the airliner Asian carriers had been buying

headline: Wal-Mart is the best stock in the Dow
text: Wal-Mart shares have about doubled in 1998, after rising some 70% in 1997, making it the best performer in the Dow Jones Industrial Average this year. Comparable-store sales are growing faster than last year, and the company bought back about 1.2 billion dollars of its own shares.
source: Wal-Mart Stores 1999 Annual Report, letter and Q&A with David Glass, https://stock.walmart.com/_assets/_46796feebc5ddf6d2adbeabac9558ae9/walmart/db/950/9626/annual_report/1999-annual-report-for-walmart-stores-inc_130199459840185623.pdf (read 2026-10-03); https://corporate.walmart.com/news/2008/11/06/wal-mart-reports-october-1998-sales (search result summary read 2026-10-03)
